pr.title: JumpThreading: fix bitwise not on non-booleans
pr.author: clubby789

issues.title: `-Zmir-opt-level` miscompiles code with panic
issues.body:
<!--
Thank you for filing a bug report! 🐛 Please provide a short summary of the bug,
along with any information you feel relevant to replicating the bug.
-->

I tried this code:

```rust
pub fn myfunc() -> i32 {
    let mut c :i32 = 1;
    c = 1 ;
    if !c != 0 {
        return 1;
    }
    panic!("Reached end of non-void function");
}

pub fn main() {
    let e = myfunc();
    println!("e={}", e);
}
```

I expected to see this happen: **always panic**

Instead, this happened: **only -Zmir-opt-level=2 panic**

For mir-opt-level 0, 1 and 3, they all normally return
```shell
% rustc -Awarnings -Zmir-opt-level=2 test.rs && ./test
thread 'main' panicked at test.rs:7:5:
Reached end of non-void function
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
%
% rustc -Awarnings -Zmir-opt-level=0 test.rs && ./test
e=1
```

analysis.summary: JumpThreading miscompiled integer `!a == b` by inverting equality polarity instead of computing the bitwise NOT of the condition value. The fix removes `Condition::inv` polarity inversion for `UnOp::Not` and evaluates `Not` on the tracked scalar constant, while making condition mapping fallible so const-eval errors discard all opportunities from that switch.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: For a non-boolean integer place, the pass rewrote a condition on `Not(a)` into the same equality value with inverted polarity, effectively turning `!a == b` into `a != b`. The regression test comment records the historical rewrite: `// Test for #131195, which was optimizing `!a == b` into `a != b`.` For example, `a = 1; if !a == 0 { 1 } else { 0 }` would take the wrong branch because `!1 == 0` is false while the polarity-inverted condition selects the true branch. The corrected logic instead evaluates the actual bitwise complement: `cond.value = self.ecx.unary_op(UnOp::Not, &ImmTy::from_scalar_int(cond.value, layout))`, and threads `bitwise_not` to the false target (`goto -> bb2`) while threading the bool `logical_not` case to the true target (`goto -> bb1`).
analysis.inputDomain: MIR for functions whose `SwitchInt` discriminant depends on an equality/inequality comparison against a `Rvalue::UnaryOp(UnOp::Not, Operand::Move(place) | Operand::Copy(place))`, where `place` has a non-boolean integer type (multi-bit) rather than `bool`. Typical source forms: `if !a == 0 { ... } else { ... }` or `if !a != 0` with an integer `a`; the same pass logic also handles bool `!a == true`.
analysis.trigger: A `SwitchInt` condition is traced backward through an assignment `lhs = Not(place)`, `state.try_get_idx(lhs, ...)` has conditions for `lhs`, and `self.map.find(place.as_ref())` succeeds. With the old code the Not branch inverts each condition's polarity; with the new code it applies `UnOp::Not` to each condition's `ScalarInt` value using the layout of `place`.
preconditions: JumpThreading is running on MIR with a switch whose condition resolves to a comparison involving a Not rvalue.
The place being negated has a layout obtainable via `self.ecx.layout_of(place.ty(self.body, self.tcx).ty)`.
The condition set for the assignment lhs is present in the threader state and the source place is found in the place map.
For the non-bool case, const-evaluation of the bitwise Not must succeed; otherwise no threading opportunity should be kept.
pitfalls: Polarity inversion (`Eq` <-> `Ne`) is only sound for `bool`; for integers greater than 1 bit the equality value must itself be complemented with `UnOp::Not`.
The patch makes `ConditionSet::map` fallible and uses `map_while`; when any condition fails it must return `None` instead of keeping a truncated/partial condition set.

When const-eval fails while walking a switch, previously discovered opportunities from that switch must be discarded: `let old_len = finder.opportunities.len();` then `finder.opportunities.truncate(old_len);`.
Do not infer the pass behavior from a retained test name or old comment; compare the decoded MIR assignments. In `bitwise_not` the corrected pass threads to `bb2` (result 0), not `bb1`.

The pre-patch base in this diff contains an early `if !place.ty(...).is_bool() { return; }` guard; the historical incorrect transformation is the underlying polarity-inversion rewrite, while the guard only suppressed it. The fix generalizes correctly by computing the Not value.
analysis.testStrategy: Use MIR-opt tests / `EMIT_MIR` on `JumpThreading`. Add `bitwise_not` with `let a = 1; if !a == 0 { 1 } else { 0 }` and verify the post-pass MIR replaces `switchInt(move _2) -> [0: bb2, otherwise: bb1]` with `goto -> bb2` (the correct false branch). Add `logical_not` with `let a = false; if !a == true { 1 } else { 0 }` and verify it becomes `goto -> bb1` (the correct true branch). Both should be checked under panic-abort and panic-unwind. Also include const-eval-error cases to ensure no partial opportunities survive (opportunities truncated to `old_len`). Do not claim the tests were executed; these are static MIR diff expectations.
evidence: // Constructing the conditions by inverting the polarity
// of equality is only correct for bools. That is to say,
// `!a == b` is not `a != b` for integers greater than 1 bit.
// Transfer the conditions on the copy rhs, after inversing polarity.
// Transfer the conditions on the copy rhs, after inverting the value of the condition.
// Test for #131195, which was optimizing `!a == b` into `a != b`.
// If we have any const-eval errors discard any opportunities found
I expected to see this happen: **always panic**
For mir-opt-level 0, 1 and 3, they all normally return
